title: What AI tools are actually good for game development?
author: Nryquellts
selftext:
I’ve been using GPT Work for a lot of stuff and I tried Claude Code too, but I keep running into this point where they’re really useful for getting something started and then once the game gets bigger they start kinda losing the plot lol.

I’ve been thinking about trying Kimi Max next, so I wanted to see what everyone else is actually using and what has worked for you.

I’m not really trying to have AI just spit out an entire game for me. I mostly use it as scaffolding. Like I have the ideas and the kind of games I want to make, then I use AI to help me get prototypes running, work through systems, fix code, organize stuff, etc. Then I go through it and keep changing things until it actually feels like something I would want to play.

Long term I wanna make weirder systems-heavy games. Monster hunting, creature anatomy and part damage, ecology, investigation, tactical combat, strange fantasy/sci-fi stuff, PS2/PS3-ish visuals, things like that. Basically games where there’s actually a lot going on under the hood instead of just throwing a bunch of content at you.

Right now I’m also trying to make and release smaller games along the way. Partly just so I actually finish things and learn from shipping them, but also because if they make anything I can put that money straight back into subscriptions, assets, software and eventually the bigger games I actually wanna make.

I figure it’s better to start making stuff now with what I have instead of waiting years until I magically know everything.

So what are you guys using right now? GPT, Claude, Kimi, Codex, Gemini, whatever. I’m especially curious what holds up once your game gets past the tiny prototype stage and you actually have to maintain the thing.

comments.author: waypostmaster
comments.body: I used Lattice to scaffold and from there has just been pure vibes. I think I’m enjoying the [reports](http://waypost.space) I’m having it produce more than the game at this point, though. They’re hilarious.

comments.author: Will_X_Intent
comments.body: Kinda songs like you need to divide your project into parts instead of having one AI so the whole thing

replies.author: Nryquellts
replies.body: Maybe, yeah, I probably need to do that, I'll work up to that point, thanks.

replies.author: Will_X_Intent
replies.body: At an example from my project, I use one AI to help me design the game, created design vision.  I had another AI helped me create the skill system.  I had another AI helped me with NPC behavior.  I'm working with another AI to design the combat.  And I'm pretty aggressive about cutting context.

replies.author: Nryquellts
replies.body: Yeah that’s kinda the point, I’m using AI as scaffolding while I learn game design by actually making stuff but thanks anyway.

replies.author: Heliaxx
replies.body: This being downvoted is goofy lol. I mean, it's not quite what the question was about, but it is important, and even adressed what OP wrote (and what's true) that AI can still only do so much past the prototype stage and you still need to be the one to know what you want, know what's going on in the code and guide it in logical steps to the desired result. And game design is part of that understanding.

comments.author: oadephon
comments.body:
I use Claude Code for everything and a little bit of Codex. 

The game hasn't turned to slop yet and it's been months. You just gotta go slowly. Add one feature at a time, make sure to get other models to review the code, test the feature yourself. Iterate, cut stuff, expand stuff. Just go slowly and think through each new feature as much as possible.

replies.author: flpcut
replies.body: This... Go slow, add context to your iterations, litteraly talk and ask for things. You're the conductor!

comments.author: CaptainAlexWest
comments.body: I just use vscode and the codex and claude plugin. It can do anything.I did custom engine stuff too. I been doing unreal engine 5.8.

comments.author: Heliaxx
comments.body:
What do you mean games? Are you just making some surface level mobile level cash Grab games? If not I guess I just don't understand what you're expecting, even with AI making a single really solid game worth playing in all the competition would take months at the very least. 

But anyways, for the tools, personally I just use claude code.

replies.author: Nryquellts
replies.body: Why feel the need to shit on me anyway? I made the game because I wanted to test something out and get advice. If you don’t like it, cool, but being weird about it doesn’t really help anybody. It’s not a cash grab, I’m not trying to trick anyone into spending money, and it’s not unplayable. If that’s what you got from the post then alright, but that wasn’t the point. If you just want to be passive aggressive about it though, cool. More engagement for me I guess.

replies.author: Heliaxx
replies.body:
? It wasn't meant as shitting on you, I don't know what kind of games you're trying to make, if browser/phone/PC/2D/3D... I just wrote what I feel like is simply the reality. You yourself wrote that AI starts having trouble when you start getting into deeper and wider with the project, and not just prototyping. And that's gonna be the case with any coding AI at this time. So I just wanted to try and give you some more reasonable expectation.

You probably won't be making any money from any sort of game made in a few weeks (which is what I felt like your post implied doing). Isn't there some single concept you're passionate about doing and that would make you stick to it? There's some stuff you won't learn just skimming the surface.

Enjoy the engagement 😄

replies.author: Nryquellts
replies.body: Yeah, I understood the actual advice. I was responding to the way you responded by calling what I’m making “surface level mobile cash grab games” when you didn’t even know what I was making. You can give advice without talking down to someone first. If that wasn’t your intention, cool, but you came across weird as hell. And yeah, thanks for the engagement lol.

replies.author: Heliaxx
replies.body:
Simply didn't understand what sort of games they were in the context of you talking about them in what felt like the span of more so weeks than months or years, with like potentially making money with them. 
Surface level mobile cash grab was simply a description as that was the only thing that came to mind with those 2 combined (and it's not even like super deragatory, most mobile games just are that, simple as, it's the business model).

replies.author: Nryquellts
replies.body: I get why you made the assumption now. I just disagree that “surface level cash grab” isn’t derogatory lol. That was pretty much the only thing I was pushing back on. I’m trying to make something decent, even if I’m experimenting and hoping it makes money. Anyway, I get what you meant now.

replies.author: Heliaxx
replies.body: Alr fair enough. Good luck with what you're doing

replies.author: Nryquellts
replies.body: Thanks, no hard feelings from my side

replies.author: waypostmaster
replies.body: Wholesome exchange, A++, would read again.

comments.author: No_Artichoke_9186
comments.body:
It helps if you actually learn what you’re doing. 

“Vibe coding” is cool but being able to actually make it work properly and being able to debug things properly is even cooler.

comments.author: Carter5on
comments.body:
Hello.  
  
Last year I was using Microsoft Copilot to help me learn GDscript in order to develop my hidden object games.  
[https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45714154](https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45714154)  
  
The graphics are handmade and they took a long time to make and be placed in the levels.  
Painted and drawn on paper > scanned > cleaned > created vector outlines in Illustrator to make the shapes stand out > exported and imported in Godot.

The sound effects and music are done with ElevenLabs.  
(I have also started using Suno for music. It is quite good.)

However, because learning to code caused me major headaches, I stopped, and I am now using ChatGPT Sol High for the coding part. I just guide it for everything, to the smallest detail. It is great for small and simple games. This summer I started using it for more complex projects that require Tech Trees, Upgrades, Buffs, AoE, RNG, and progression.  
  
It's been great so far. It helps having professional experience in games development and game design and understanding that goes into a game. This is my portfolio: [https://www.artstation.com/carterson](https://www.artstation.com/carterson)

I am now experimenting with providing ChatGPT all the 2D/3D graphics and assets of my games, and asking it to compile them into builds based on all we have discussed, so that I don't have to go into UE5. 

In my case Claude didn't work out for games and apps so I dropped it. It often refused to follow instructions and my tokens ran out a few times during the day. I had to buy extra tokens once or twice during the day to do my job.  
  
I got fed up with it, so I picked ChatGPT. I have never run out of tokens and I am using it aggressively every day for both my job and my games. I believe ChatGPT Sol will help you with your weirder systems. It shows great results for me.  
  
I had Free Kimi, but it was very often giving me "high traffic right now" (or something like that) errors and I never got to do any real work.

I hope this helped you a little bit.
